 Judgment

Wife, children and parents of Muralidhara B.H. filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 asserting that on 13.05.2023 at 10.30 p.m. when Muralidhara B.H. and others are travelling by sitting in a Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 on Hennur- Bengaluru road, from Bilishivale towards Devanahalli

, in front of Anjana bar, Hosur Bande, Bengaluru, driver of Car drove the same negligently, made the car to turn turtle, thereby caused the accident, caused instantaneous death of Muralidhara B.H.
2.
Regarding accident Devanahalli traffic police registered a case in crime No.107/2023 against the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436.
3. As on the date of accident Muralidhara B.H. being aged 34 years, used to earn Rs.30,000/p.m. by working as Driver, used to contribute the entire income to the family.

4. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their Advocates filed separate written statements denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident , age occupation ,income of the deceased.

Asha.V vs Anand Raj.C on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13847336/
2 5.

On the basis of the pleadings on 15.02.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, on 13.05.2023 at about 10.30 p.m. in front of Anjana Bar, Hosur Bande, Bengaluru city, the death caused to one Muralidhara B.H.
was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.
No. KA-04-MN- 6436 as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation ? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

6. On 07.03.2024, 12.08.2024, petitioner No.1- Asha/wife of the deceased Muralidhara B.H.
deposed as PW1 and produced 20 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.20.
7.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioner and respondent No.2 and perused the records.

8. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.37,09,000/- with current and future interest at 6%p..a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence PW1- Smt. Asha W/o Muralidhara B.H. stated that on 13.05.2023 at 10.30 p.m. when Muralidhara B.H. and others are travelling by sitting in a Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 on Hennur- Bengaluru road, from Bilishivale towards Devanahalli, in front of Anjana bar, Hosur Bande, Bengaluru, driver of Car drove the same negligently, made the car to turn turtle, thereby caused the accident, caused instantaneous death of Muralidhara B.H.
10.
In the written statement respondent No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident .
11. In the cross-examination, PW1 stated that she never witnessed the accident.

12. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.107/2023 registered by Devanahalli traffic police against Dhanush the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04- MN-6436 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC regarding the accident taken place on 13.05.2023 at 10.30 p.m. on the basis of the complaint filed by petitioner No.5 Hanumanthappa S/o.
Late Munishamappa.
Ex . P.2
is the copy of the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Asha.V vs Anand Raj.

C on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13847336/
3
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the vehicle seizure mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident.
Ex.P.7 is the motor vehicle accident report.
Ex.P.8 is the copy of PM report.
Ex.P.9 is the copy of Inquest report.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Devanahalli Traffic Police in Crime No.123/2023 against Dhanush S/o Late Anjanappa - driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC .The
enclosures of charge sheet are statements of Dhananjay S/o Venkateshappa, Manoj Kumar S/o Muniyappa, Shashikumar B.T. S/o Thirumalappa, Madhu S/o Chikkapaiaha, Rajesh P.S. S/o Puttaraju.
In the police records name of Muralidhara B.H. is noted as one of the inmate of Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 and victim of accident.
13. In this case the respondents have not placed any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

14. Hence, I have concluded that on 13.05.2023 at 10.30 p.m. when Muralidhara B.H. and others are travelling by sitting in a Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 on Hennur- Bengaluru road, from Bilishivale towards Devanahalli, in front of Anjana bar, Hosur Bande, Bengaluru, Dhanush S/o Late Anjanappa driver of Car drove the same negligently, made the car to turn turtle, thereby caused the accident, caused instantaneous death of Muralidhara B.H.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

15. Issue No.2: In the evidence PW1-Asha W/o Muralidhara B.H. stated that as on the date of accident her husband deceased Muralidhara B.H. being aged about 34 years, used to earn Rs.30,000/p.m. by working as Driver, used to contribute entire income to the family.
16. In the written statement respondent No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of the deceased.

17. In the cross-examination PW1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident Muralidhara never earning Rs.30,000/- per month (wrongly typed as Rs.40,000/- per month).
18.
In the copy of Aadhaar card and driving licence marked at Ex.P.11 and P.17 the date of birth of Muralidhara B.H. is noted as 25.04.1989.
The Driving Licence marked at Ex.P.17 shows that since 05.01.2010 Muralidhara had licence to drive light motor vehicle/motorcycle with gear.
19. The copies of the Aadhar card shows that petitioners are the wife, children and parents of Muralidhara B.H..
In the file there are no evidence to show the income of the deceased Muralidhara.

20. Hence I have calculated the compensation under the head of loss of dependency in the following terms:
Age of the deceased Muralidhara B.H. as on 34 years the date of accident - Notional income of the deceased Muralidhara - Rs.16,000/- B.H. as on the date of accident Add: 50% future prospects - Rs.24,000/- (Rs.16000 + 50% (8,000) =
Asha.V vs Anand Raj.C on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13847336/
4 24,000) Less : 1/ 4th towards personal expenses of Rs.18,000/-
the deceased Muralidhara B.H. (24,000 - 6,000/- = 18,000) Loss of dependency 18,000x12x16 Rs.34,56,000/-
21.
Hence, I award Rs.34,56,000/- towards loss of dependency.

Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.2,20,000/- (44,000 x5) towards consortium.

22. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners being wife, children and parents of deceased Muralidhara B.H. are entitle to receive Rs.37,09,000/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. as compensation from the respondents.
Sl. No.
Head of Compensation Amount/
Rs 1. Loss of dependency 34,56,000-00 2. Loss of estate 16,500-00 3.
Funeral expenses 16,500-00 4.
Loss of Consortium to 2,20,000-00 petitioners No.1 to 4 at Rs.44,000/each Total 37,09,000-00
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly.
23. Issue No.3:
In the written statement respondent No.2 admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 as on the date of accident.
In the reply to notice at Ex.P.6 submitted by owner of the car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 -Harish N. S/o Nagaraju to I.O.
has noted the DL number of Dhanush S/o Anjanappa.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident respondent No.1 owner of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MN- 6436 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents No.1 and 2 to pay compensation to the petitioners,
Hence, I answer issue No.3 and pass the following :
ORDER The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
The respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.37,09,000/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MN-6436 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally .

Asha.V vs Anand Raj.C on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13847336/
5

After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioners No.1- Asha, Petitioner No.4- Gowramma and petitioner No.5- Hanumanthappa may be released by crediting the same to their bank accounts directly.

Entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioners No.2- Kavyashree, petitioner No.3- Darshan (minors) shall be deposited in any bank in their names till they attain the age of 19 years without permitting to create any encumbrances and reserving liberty to their mother petitioner No.1/guardian to withdraw periodical interest once in 3 months in accordance with law.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 10th day of January, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
